smallholdings.name: Smallholdings
smallholdings.flavor: A hedge, a cow, and a name on the roll.
smallholdings.text: Worked farms and pastures gain +1 food and +1 gold.

expansionistGranaryLevies.name: Granary Levies
expansionistGranaryLevies.flavor: A new mouth arrives with two hands.
expansionistGranaryLevies.text: When a city grows in population, gain 15 production

theGrovesAndTheStones.name: The Groves and the Stones
theGrovesAndTheStones.flavor: The old trees stood here before the altar did, and knew it.
theGrovesAndTheStones.text: Unimproved forests gain +1 faith, in a city with a Shrine.

theNaturalists.name: The Naturalists
theNaturalists.flavor: They counted everything and ate none of it.
theNaturalists.text: Each city gains +1 science for each distinct feature type it works. Your capital gains +1 science.

claimByTheSpade.name: Claim by the Spade
claimByTheSpade.flavor: The border is wherever the ditch ends.
claimByTheSpade.text: Improving unclaimed land beside your border claims it for the nearest eligible city. Each hex first claimed this way grants that city 15 food and 10 gold. [Improvement-led claim.]
claimByTheSpade.note: A worker cannot yet build outside your borders, and nothing takes ground in for the town that reaches it.
deferred: works raised on open ground beside your border take that ground for the nearest town
the first claim of each place pays that town in grain and coin

theGrowingAnnals.name: The Growing Annals
theGrowingAnnals.flavor: Every birth is entered, and the ink is never dry.
theGrowingAnnals.text: While active, gains +1 science and +1 culture per turn whenever one of your cities grows in population, no cap.
deferred: the card keeps count of every citizen born and pays a little more each turn for it
theGrowingAnnals.note: Not built, and the one thing missing is small. A town remembers how many people live in it and not how many ever did, and the design pays only for growth past a town's own greatest — so a counter of plain growth would write the annals twice for one citizen a levy took and the fields gave back. A town's high-water mark is one number on the town and one comparison where it grows; the counter of growths waits on it and on nothing else.

thePatientHarvest.name: The Patient Harvest
thePatientHarvest.flavor: The granary waits better than the barracks does.
thePatientHarvest.text: Cities retain 30% of the food spent on growth, but produce military units 15% more slowly.

thePioneersPortion.name: The Pioneers' Portion
thePioneersPortion.flavor: Send them out fed, or do not send them.
thePioneersPortion.text: +25% production toward settlers. A city founded beside a resource costs one less authority.
thePioneersPortion.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. Nothing yet prices a town by what its ground carries.
deferred: a town founded beside a resource asks less of your writ than any other
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theFieldAltars.name: The Field Altars
theFieldAltars.flavor: Where the good things grow, something is thanked.
theFieldAltars.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready; the card is not.
deferred: the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

levyOfTheLand.name: Levy of the Land
levyOfTheLand.flavor: The field gives up a son and calls it a harvest.
levyOfTheLand.text: Cities may spend one citizen to gain production equal to ten turns of their food. A city may levy once every five turns. [Population-payment action.]
levyOfTheLand.note: A city cannot yet spend a citizen on anything. The verb, its waiting period and its payment are all still to be built.
deferred: a city spends one of its people and is paid in labour for it
a city may do this only now and then

plantedForests.name: Planted Forests
plantedForests.flavor: We put the wood back, row by row.
plantedForests.text: Workers may plant forest on eligible open land for one charge. It matures after fifteen turns. [Planting and maturity.]
plantedForests.note: Held whole, and waiting on planting. Nothing may plant a wood, and a wood nobody planted has stood since the world was made — so there is no turn to write on it and nothing to measure a young one against. The planter is what makes a wood young; until one exists, neither half of this can be said.
deferred: a worker plants a wood on open ground of your own
a planted wood is young for a long while, and cannot be felled for timber until it is grown

expansionistTinkersGuild.name: Tinkers' Guild
expansionistTinkersGuild.flavor: Nothing is worn out while a tinker is awake.
expansionistTinkersGuild.text: Workers you produce or purchase gain +1 charge.

thePrizeRolls.name: The Prize Rolls
thePrizeRolls.flavor: The herald lists what nobody else has.
thePrizeRolls.text: +1 renown for every unique luxury resource.
thePrizeRolls.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready; the card is not.
deferred: the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

oldGrowth.name: Old Growth
oldGrowth.flavor: These trunks were old when the road was new.
oldGrowth.text: Worked mature forests gain +1 food and +1 production. Chopping mature forest grants 50% more production.
oldGrowth.note: Held whole, and waiting on planting. A hex now remembers when its works were raised, but a wood is not a work: one nobody planted has stood since the world was made, so nothing can tell a grown wood from a young one until something plants one.
deferred: a grown wood your people work feeds and builds better than a young one
felling a grown wood yields more timber than felling a young one

charcoalBurners.name: Charcoal Burners
charcoalBurners.flavor: Smoke goes up, and somebody calls it prayer.
charcoalBurners.text: Chopping forest or jungle also grants faith and culture each equal to 20% of its chop production.

theWoodlandEdge.name: The Woodland Edge
theWoodlandEdge.flavor: The best field is the one the wood still watches.
theWoodlandEdge.text: Worked ordinary improvements beside unimproved forest gain +1 production per adjacent forest, at most +2. Worked unimproved forests beside a farm gain +2 food, once per forest.
theWoodlandEdge.note: Held whole. A hex can be paid a helping for every wood in its ring now, but the works this card pays are the ordinary ones — and an improvement that is not a great person's work is a thing no ground condition can name.
deferred: works pay more for every wild wood standing next to them
a wild wood beside a field feeds better for it

theHighPastures.name: The High Pastures
theHighPastures.flavor: Above the last wall, the grass is ours.
theHighPastures.text: Your cities may work owned mountains within their work radius. Those mountains provide 3 production and 2 faith. [Workability exception, not movement permission.]
theHighPastures.note: No law can yet put a citizen on a mountain: what a town may work is a fact about the ground alone.
deferred: your people may work the mountains inside your borders
a worked mountain gives stone and devotion

theWatercourses.name: The Watercourses
theWatercourses.flavor: The river is only lent; the ditch is owned.
theWatercourses.text: Farms directly beside a river irrigate adjacent farms. Irrigated worked farms gain +1 production. Water does not relay beyond that first step. [Farm-water adjacency.]
theWatercourses.note: A field either stands on fresh water or it does not; no field can yet pass water to the next one.
deferred: a field on the river waters the fields beside it
a watered field builds better
the water goes no further than one field over

theMusterOfTheFields.name: The Muster of the Fields
theMusterOfTheFields.flavor: Put down the sickle and pick up the other thing.
theMusterOfTheFields.text: Cities may spend one citizen to muster their best legally available melee unit. This shares the city's five-turn levy limit. [Population payment; normal technology and resource access.]
theMusterOfTheFields.note: A city cannot yet spend a citizen on anything. A card may raise a soldier on the calendar, but never in exchange for a person.
deferred: a city spends one of its people and stands up the best soldier it could raise
a city may do this only now and then, and not while it is levying for labour

theLandShapesUs.name: The Land Shapes Us
theLandShapesUs.flavor: Ask where a town was founded and you have asked everything.
theLandShapesUs.text: Cities gain their founding trait: river +3 food/+3 gold; coast +1 route capacity; hill +3 production/+3 defence; forest +3 science; desert +4 faith; tundra/snow +4 culture; plain +2 food/+2 production. Exactly one trait applies.
theLandShapesUs.note: Nothing writes down what kind of place a town was founded on, so nothing can give it one reward and refuse it the rest.
deferred: every town remembers the one kind of place it was founded on
each kind of place pays its town its own reward, and only ever one of them

theOldSongs.name: The Old Songs
theOldSongs.flavor: Unploughed ground keeps the older tunes.
theOldSongs.note: Open water your people work counts as unbuilt ground here: the game tells works from wild, and not land from sea.

theLocalCensus.name: The Local Census
theLocalCensus.flavor: Count the working hands; the rest is opinion.
theLocalCensus.text: Gain +1 authority capacity for every two cities working at least four land tiles, at most +3.
theLocalCensus.note: A card may count your towns, but not yet only the ones whose people work a stated amount of ground.
deferred: your writ is widened by every second town that works a real stretch of country

theWorksShadow.name: The Work's Shadow
theWorksShadow.flavor: Great work throws a long shade, and things grow in it.
theWorksShadow.text: +1 culture on tiles adjacent to a great work.
theWorksShadow.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready; the card is not.
deferred: ground beside a great one's work sings for it
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theOpenFurlongs.name: The Open Furlongs
theOpenFurlongs.text: Farms gain +1 production for every two adjacent farm tiles.
theOpenFurlongs.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished, and marked uncertain there. A hex is paid a helping for every field beside it now, but not for every second one of them.
deferred: a field builds better for every second field beside it
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theProvincialSchools.name: The Provincial Schools
theProvincialSchools.flavor: The seam is opened, and then explained.
theProvincialSchools.text: +1 science and +1 culture on improved resource tiles in cities with a national building.
theProvincialSchools.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready — the realm's single great houses can be named now — and the card is not.
deferred: worked seams teach and sing in a town that has raised an empire building
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theCuratorsRoll.name: The Curators' Roll
theCuratorsRoll.flavor: Somebody must know what the city keeps.
theCuratorsRoll.text: +1 renown for each great work worked by a city.
theCuratorsRoll.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The kinds of great one's work a town puts to use can be counted now, but a standing trickle counts the realm's towns and not the ground inside one.
deferred: your standing grows with every great one's work your towns put to use
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theCommonTreasury.name: The Common Treasury
theCommonTreasury.flavor: What one town spends, the road repays to all.
theCommonTreasury.text: A production levy also grants each other connected owned city production equal to 20% of the levy's original payout. Shared production cannot trigger another sharing payout.
theCommonTreasury.note: A city cannot yet spend a citizen on anything, so there is no levy for this to follow.
deferred: a levy of labour pays every other town joined to your capital a share of what it raised
what is shared out cannot be shared again

irrigationWorks.name: Irrigation Works
irrigationWorks.flavor: Water goes where it is told, once.
irrigationWorks.text: Workers may build irrigation works for one charge on eligible owned open land. Adjacent farms count as irrigated and gain +1 food when worked. irrigation works base yield: +1 food +1 science [New improvement; ordinary tile/resource restrictions apply.]
irrigationWorks.note: There is no such works to build, and no field can yet pass water to the next one.
deferred: a worker raises a waterworks on open ground of your own
fields beside it count as watered and feed better
the waterworks itself feeds and teaches

reclamation.name: Reclamation
reclamation.flavor: Cut it down and the ground forgets it was jungle.
reclamation.text: Clearing jungle changes its land to plains and grants 30 food in addition to normal chop production. [Underlying-terrain change; does not change hills or resources.]
reclamation.note: The ground under a wood never changes in this game. The worksheet is reworking this card besides.
deferred: clearing a jungle leaves open plain behind it
clearing a jungle fills the granary as well as the woodpile

theCoppice.name: The Coppice
theCoppice.flavor: Take the crown, leave the stool.
theCoppice.text: Chopping mature forest you planted leaves young forest standing. It matures again after fifteen turns and cannot be harvested while young.
theCoppice.note: Held whole, and waiting on planting. A wood cannot be planted, and nothing regrows where one is felled — this card is the second half of a cycle whose first half does not exist.
deferred: felling a wood you planted leaves a young wood standing where it was
the young wood grows back in time, and gives no timber until it has

theHermitages.name: The Hermitages
theHermitages.flavor: He wanted nothing, and the ground gave it anyway.
theHermitages.text: Great-person works qualify for your unimproved-land card bonuses. Each great-person work also grants adjacent worked tiles +2 of each of its positive native yield types. [Native yields exclude card additions; no propagation.]
theHermitages.note: No card can change what another card's ground condition admits.
deferred: a great one's work counts as wild ground for your other laws
ground beside a great one's work shares in whatever that work provides

expansionistTheOldWays.name: The Old Ways
expansionistTheOldWays.flavor: Leave it alone and it pays you.
expansionistTheOldWays.text: Worked unimproved land gains +2 food and +2 gold. Worked ordinary improvements lose 1 production, to a minimum of zero. Great-person works are exempt from this penalty.
expansionistTheOldWays.note: A law may take from a hex, but nothing yet stops the taking at nothing, so ground with no labour in it would fall below nothing.
deferred: works lose a little labour, and never fall below nothing for it

theHighlands.name: The Highlands
theHighlands.flavor: Every seam in the hill is a lesson.
theHighlands.text: mines and quarries on hills gain +2 science and +1 production.

theSteppe.name: The Steppe
theSteppe.text: pastures gain +2 production. Horse-dependent military units cost 25% less production.
theSteppe.note: The horse-dependent soldiers are the mounted ones the roster draws, ridden and shooting alike.

theFloodplains.name: The Floodplains
theFloodplains.flavor: The flood is a creditor who pays first.
theFloodplains.text: floodplain farms gain additional food equal to their native food yield before card additions and multipliers.
theFloodplains.note: A share of what a hex's own ground provides reaches every voice it speaks in at once, and this card means the grain alone. The worksheet is reworking the figure besides.
deferred: a field on the floodplain is paid again in grain for the grain its ground already gives

theCoast.name: The Coast
theCoast.flavor: The sea is a field nobody has to plough.
theCoast.text: Worked fishing boats gain +2 food and +2 culture.

provincialCouncils.name: Provincial Councils
provincialCouncils.flavor: The province speaks, and is not always wrong.
provincialCouncils.text: Each connected noncapital city working at least four land tiles grants +1 authority capacity, at most +8, and gains +1 happiness.
provincialCouncils.note: A card may ask whether a town is joined to the capital and whether it is the capital, but not yet whether its people work a stated amount of ground.
deferred: only the towns whose people work a real stretch of country are counted

expansionistTheGrainDole.name: The Grain Dole
expansionistTheGrainDole.flavor: A fed city forgets what it was angry about.
expansionistTheGrainDole.text: Cities of at least ten population gain +4 happiness and retain an additional 20% of food spent on growth.

theStandingPatronage.name: The Standing Patronage
theStandingPatronage.flavor: The master's works are the crown's furniture.
theStandingPatronage.text: While slotted, this card gains +1 authority for every great person improvement created. Starts at +1 authority.
theStandingPatronage.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. A card may keep a running count of battles, of wonders and of coin spent, but not yet of the great ones' works.
deferred: the card keeps count of every great one's work raised while it sits, and widens your writ for each
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theWoodsmensMarch.name: The Woodsmen's March
theWoodsmensMarch.flavor: The trees are on our side, or near enough.
theWoodsmensMarch.text: Units gain additional +4 combat strength while fighting in either forest or hills (does not stack on forested hills). Units ignore terrain penalties from moving onto forest or hills.
theWoodsmensMarch.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. A strength line may be paid for hills and not for woods, and nothing excuses a column the cost of rough ground.
deferred: your soldiers fight harder in the woods and on the hills, and never for both at once
your soldiers walk into woods and hills for what open ground would cost
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theQuarterOfMasters.name: The Quarter of Masters
theQuarterOfMasters.flavor: Put two masters on one street and watch.
theQuarterOfMasters.text: Great works with an adjacent great work gain double yields. This never stacks.
theQuarterOfMasters.note: A provisional name for a line the worksheet has not finished. The rule itself is ready; the card is not.
deferred: a great one's work standing beside another pays twice over, however many stand there
the name, the rarity and the wording are the designer's to settle

theWoodwrights.name: The Woodwrights
theWoodwrights.flavor: Timber is patience, taken all at once.
theWoodwrights.text: Forest and jungle chops grant 100% more production. Chop percentages add together before Charcoal Burners reads the payout.

theComplementaryProvinces.name: The Complementary Provinces
theComplementaryProvinces.flavor: Nobody is rich in one thing.
theComplementaryProvinces.text: Connected cities gain +5% production and +5% culture per different founding trait represented among your connected cities, at most +30% each. The Land Shapes Us need not be owned.
theComplementaryProvinces.note: Nothing writes down what kind of place a town was founded on, so nothing can tell how many different kinds your realm holds.
deferred: your joined towns build and sing better for every different kind of place your realm was founded on

theVariedCountry.name: The Varied Country
theVariedCountry.flavor: A table with one dish on it is not a table.
theVariedCountry.text: Cities working at least four distinct terrain or feature types gain +20% food, production, gold and culture.
theVariedCountry.note: Nothing counts how many different kinds of country a town works.
deferred: a town whose people work many different kinds of country prospers in every voice at once

theCommonDomain.name: The Common Domain
theCommonDomain.flavor: The commons runs to where the walking stops.
theCommonDomain.text: Cities may work owned land one hex beyond their normal work radius and lock two additional tiles. This grants neither citizens nor ownership.
theCommonDomain.note: How far a town may reach, and how many hexes its governor may hold aside, are both fixed and cannot yet be widened by a law.
deferred: your towns work their own ground one step further out than other towns do
your governors may hold aside more hexes than other governors may

seasonalLevies.name: Seasonal Levies
seasonalLevies.flavor: Take them in the winter and give the spring back.
seasonalLevies.text: After spending a citizen on either levy, that city gains +40% food for ten turns. Repeated levies refresh the duration; they do not stack it. Regrowth triggers no historical-growth reward.
seasonalLevies.note: A city cannot yet spend a citizen on anything, so there is no levy for this to follow.
deferred: a town that has spent one of its people is fed better for a while afterwards
spending another refreshes the season rather than lengthening it

theHarvestTithe.name: The Harvest Tithe
theHarvestTithe.flavor: The tenth sheaf, and the wild hedge that grew it.
theHarvestTithe.text: Worked farms beside unimproved land gain +3 gold, once per farm. Farms beside a mature unimproved forest also gain +2 production.
theHarvestTithe.note: Half built, and so held whole. A field beside wild ground can be paid for it, but a wood nobody planted has stood since the world was made — so the second half waits on planting, which is what makes a wood young enough to tell a grown one from.
deferred: a field beside wild ground is worth coin for it
a field beside a grown wild wood builds better besides

forestSanctuaries.name: Forest Sanctuaries
forestSanctuaries.text: Worked mature unimproved forests gain +2 culture and +2 faith. Cities working at least three demand 20% less population happiness.
forestSanctuaries.note: Held whole, on two counts. A wood nobody planted has stood since the world was made, so nothing can tell a grown one from a young one until planting exists — and nothing admits a town for the number of wild woods its people work.
deferred: a grown wild wood your people work sings and prays for you
a town working several of them asks less of your peace

theLandsGreatWork.name: The Land's Great Work
theLandsGreatWork.flavor: The harvest raises the monument, and the monument eats the harvest.
theLandsGreatWork.text: A city constructing an empire building, world wonder or the Opus gains production equal to 50% of its base food surplus. Military production in all your cities is reduced by 20%.
theLandsGreatWork.note: A share of a town's grain is read off everything it grows, not off what is left after its people have eaten, and the game keeps no shelf of empire buildings to ask about.
deferred: a town raising a great building turns a share of the grain its people do not eat into labour
